item.title: Hi JobStash subscriber, It's DuckDegen, or David as I'm known IRL. I'm the found
item.description:
Hi JobStash subscriber,

It's DuckDegen, or David as I'm known IRL. I'm the founder of JobStash.

This is my first email to you in four years, and my last from JobStash. On Sunday, 22 November, I'm shutting JobStash.xyz down.

Its websites will go offline that day. Its Telegram channel will stop posting jobs.

I built JobStash back in 2022 because I needed a job myself. It was supposed to be a 3 month experiment, but here we are, 4 years later. Back then, I wanted one place where I could see who was hiring and get deep insights about the opportunities at hand, which is information most recruiters simply didn't know or were willing to share.

I kept JobStash online for free and never ran ads because I believed that JobStash can be run as a public good which is funded by grants and by data services which do not depend on deceiving users. I did my earnest best to upkeep this until the very end. Nearly 12,000 of you signed up. We tracked 57490 jobs at more than 2,000 organizations, and you all sent more than 60,000 job applications facilitated by JobStash.

All told, JobStash cost about $370,000 to build and run. Some of it came from Optimism RetroPGF, some of it from GitCoin, some of it from ThankArb, and lots of infra costs were covered by GCP grants. Back in 2024 we could use grant funding to sustain ourselves instead of having to rely on the pay-for-placement or pay-for-job-ads model that all other job boards relied on, allowing us to build a job board that was truly neutral, unbiased and which refreshingly put the job seeker first. But the grants dried up and the funding got spent.

For the past two years, I've paid every bill out of my own pocket because I wanted everyone in this industry to keep using JobStash for free, and because I made the bet that talent teams would need our data driven insights into who's who, and who's safe to hire. That bet was wrong.

I can't afford to keep funding the infra anymore, and JobStash has consumed thousands of hours of my time. I'm now out of work again. You can find my CV here if you wish to hire me: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1iUEsS7nR9MKU3nvaPXPt4gnqkPfXnQnOhZ-r4_bjJgI

Please be there for each other. If a friend or peer is looking for work, check in on them. Ask how they're doing, share a role that might suit them, or offer an introduction. Make time to listen, even if you don't have a solution. Knowing that someone cares can mean a lot when things are difficult.

And if you're the one having a hard time, reach out to your friends and peers. Tell them what you need, whether that's an introduction, advice or someone to talk to. We all need others to be there for us sometimes. When you can be that person for someone else, please do.

And to everyone who ever wrote to me about JobStash, thank you. Some of you sent just a heart emoji. You had your own job hunt to worry about and you still took a minute to encourage me. It meant a lot to be the guy who got to read those notes. Thank you for keeping me motivated and feeling loved.

If you'd like to work through your search with me, I'm offering two services:

Career Coaching Session - $150
A 60-minute conversation about where you're getting stuck and what to try next. We can look at the kinds of roles you're pursuing, how you're presenting your experience, and how to approach people in your network. You'll leave with a practical plan for your next steps.

CV and LinkedIn audit - $250
We'll work through your experience together, then I'll rewrite your CV and help update your LinkedIn profile to make your work and achievements easier to understand.

A stronger CV won't guarantee an interview. But it gives people a clearer picture of what you've done.

If either would be helpful, reply to this email and tell me a little about what you're looking for.

It's been an honour to run JobStash for you, and to work with stellar talent like https://x.com/AndySakov and https://x.com/johnshift_ and my late cofounder https://x.com/enricobach.

David Leonardi

@duckdegen here and on X (https://x.com/duckdegen)
